title: Agreement can displace accuracy
claim: The studied assistants sometimes favored responses aligned with a user’s views over truthful answers.
limit: This is evidence about the tested tasks and systems. It does not establish a failure rate for every current model or validate Human Signal.

title: Remembering includes updating
claim: LongMemEval tests extraction, reasoning across sessions and time, knowledge updates, and abstention.
limit: Benchmark performance is not a guarantee of faithful personal continuity, appropriate disclosure, or permission to use a memory.

title: Relevant is not always appropriate
claim: A benchmark using synthetic profiles tests whether systems disclose remembered attributes in appropriate task contexts. It reports contextual-integrity violations in tested systems.
limit: Synthetic benchmark conditions do not establish the prevalence of real-world harm or prove that this site’s proposed boundary design works.

title: Use, attachment, and wellbeing
by: Fang et al. · revised October 2025 preprint
claim: In a four-week study with 981 participants, the revised report found no significant effects of assigned interaction conditions. Greater voluntary use was associated with worse psychosocial outcomes.
limit: The usage association does not establish that more use caused those outcomes. This is not a diagnosis, a universal effect, or a validation of Anti-Attachment.

title: Accountability needs more than a trace
claim: The profile organizes generative-AI risks and management actions, including human–AI configuration and information integrity.
limit: A risk framework guides evaluation. Citing it is not certification, compliance, or proof of an architecture’s safety.

title: Make correction possible
claim: The authors propose and evaluate 18 guidelines for human–AI interaction, including support for correction and control over time.
limit: Design guidance informs our choices. Whether a specific interface improves agency still needs evaluation.
